claim.pdf_says: '14.5.2   Conditional phrase' and '14.5.3   Scope of statements' are printed as third-level clause headings, siblings of '14.5.1   General' (page 562); '14.5.3.1   General', '14.5.3.2   Explicit scope termination' and '14.5.3.3   Implicit scope termination' are their fourth-level children.
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.5.2 Conditional phrase / ## 14.5.3 Scope of statements / ### 14.5.3.1 General / ### 14.5.3.2 Explicit scope termination / ### 14.5.3.3 Implicit scope termination   (while the sibling '### 14.5.1 General' on page 562 sits one level deeper)
claim.why_it_matters: 14.5.2 and 14.5.3 are emitted at the same level as their own parent '## 14.5 Procedural statements and sentences', so the outline shows them as peers of 14.5 instead of children, and 14.5.1 ends up nested one level deeper than its own siblings. The whole scope-of-statements subtree — the normative basis for explicit and implicit scope termination — is mis-parented.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on three independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The claim is filed as kind='missing-heading', but all five headings are present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md with byte-exact numbers and titles: '14.5.2 Conditional phrase' (line 23628), '14.5.3 Scope of statements' (23635), '14.5.3.1 General' (23638), '14.5.3.2 Explicit scope termination' (23643), '14.5.3.3 Implicit scope termination' (23654). Each carries a correct anchor ( etc.), and the normative body text under every one of them matches the rendered page word for word — including the two-part explicit-terminator list ('the most-recently preceding unterminated statement...' / 'any unterminated statements that appear between...'). No text, no heading, and no clause number was lost. The filed kind does not describe anything that happened. (2) THE PDF MAKES NO LEVEL DISTINCTION TO LOSE. I rendered p565 and p562 at 300 dpi and looked at the printed glyphs. On p562, '14.3 Declaratives', '14.4 Procedures', '14.4.1 General', '14.4.2 Sections', '14.4.3 Paragraphs', '14.5 Procedural statements and sentences' and '14.5.1 General' are set in one identical style: same bold face, same point size, same flush-left margin, same space above. On p565, '14.5.2 Conditional phrase', '14.5.3 Scope of statements', '14.5.3.1 General', '14.5.3.2 Explicit scope termination' and '14.5.3.3 Implicit scope termination' are set in that same single style. ISO does not typeset clause depth here — a depth-2, depth-3 and depth-4 heading are visually indistinguishable on the page. The claim's premise that the PDF 'prints them as third-level clause headings' is an inference from the decimal number, not an observation of the page. The hierarchy is carried entirely by the decimal clause numbering, and the transcription reproduces that numbering exactly. Nothing the PDF actually encodes was dropped. (3) IT IS A DOCUMENT-WIDE TRANSCRIPTION ARTIFACT, NOT A PAGE-565 DEFECT. Cross-tabulating clause depth against markdown '#' depth over all 2098 numbered headings in the file shows the mapping is noise everywhere: depth-3 clauses are emitted as '##' 276 times and '###' 508 times; depth-4 clauses as '###' 620 times, '##' 162 times, '####' 24 times; depth-5 as '##' 118, '###' 128, '####' 41. The same inconsistency sits three lines above the disputed text in the same chapter ('### 14.1', '### 14.2', '#### 14.2.1', '## 14.2.2', '## 14.3', '## 14.4', '### 14.4.1') and repeats in chapter 13 ('## 13.10.4' beside '### 13.10.3', '## 13.15.3' beside '### 13.15.2'). Markdown '#' depth in this transcription is not a hierarchy signal anywhere in the document, so any consumer must key on the decimal number — which is intact. Ledgering p565 as a structural content discrepancy would misattribute a global formatting characteristic to one page and imply a normative loss that did not occur. Markdown heading depth is presentation, the meaning-bearing hierarchy (the clause number) is preserved verbatim, and a reader resolving §14.5.3.2 gets identical normative text from either source. This is the 'only formatting / does not change meaning' rejection case.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. All five headings and all their normative body text are present and verbatim-correct in the markdown; nothing is missing, so the filed kind 'missing-heading' is wrong on its face. The sole difference is markdown '#' nesting depth, which (a) corresponds to no distinction the PDF itself draws — clause levels 2, 3 and 4 share one identical bold heading style on the printed page, verified at 300 dpi on both p562 and p565 — and (b) is inconsistent across the whole transcription, not just here: of 2098 numbered headings, depth-3 clauses are emitted as '##' 276x and '###' 508x, depth-4 as '###' 620x and '##' 162x. If the owner wants uniform outline nesting, that is one document-wide normalization pass keyed off the decimal clause number, not a per-page spec-reconciliation finding, and it carries zero normative risk.
